texts: Patients with normal preoperative PA pressures are not at particular risk of postoperative pulmonary hypertension: D.

Pulmonary hypertensive crises after surgery are most likely when the pulmonary arteries are reactive or remodelled: neonatal repair, obstructed total anomalous pulmonary venous return, large shunts repaired late in an older child, and Down syndrome.
Bypass itself can trigger a crisis through endothelial injury and inflammation, and suctioning, pain or hypoxia can set one off.
In the picture, only the child whose gauge sat calmly in the green before the operation stays calm.
Memory hook: a calm gauge before stays calm after.
